# Lavendar Lewis

## Overview

- **Age:** Forty-five years old  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034), [v2 c21 P44](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0044)</sub>
- **Origin:** East Grafton  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Miss Lavendar  <sub>[v2 c21 P40](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0040), [v2 c21 P44](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0044)</sub>

## Appearance

Miss Lavendar is a small, thin lady with snow-white, thick, beautifully wavy hair styled in becoming puffs and coils. Beneath her white hair she has an almost girlish, pink-cheeked face with dimples and big, soft, wood-brown eyes with golden glints. She wears dainty cream muslin dresses adorned with pale roses.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P44](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0044), [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045), [v2 c22 P2](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0002), [v2 c26 P56](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0056)_

## Personality

Miss Lavendar is romantic, imaginative, and considered peculiar by local community standards due to her secluded lifestyle. She possesses an ineradicable youthfulness at heart, enjoying games, imaginary companion stories, and sweet delights. Beneath her bright, naturally charming, and sensible exterior, she harbors a deep capacity for affection and quiet vulnerability regarding her past.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P33](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0033), [v2 c21 P35](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0035), [v2 c21 P87](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0087), [v2 c22 P3](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0003), [v2 c23 P29](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0029), [v2 c27 P63](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0063)_

## Traits

- Imaginative  <sub>[v2 c27 P63](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0063)</sub>
- Romantic  <sub>[v2 c23 P29](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0029)</sub>
- Peculiar  <sub>[v2 c21 P32](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0032), [v2 c22 P3](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0003)</sub>

## Abilities

- Storytelling and imaginary world building  <sub>[v2 c27 P63](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0063)</sub>

## History

Miss Lavendar lived for many years in seclusion at Echo Lodge, an old stone house surrounded by firs and Grafton River meadows. Living out of the public eye, she entertained herself with imaginary companions, including a 'little dream-boy,' assisted by her young handmaiden, Charlotta the Fourth. When Anne Shirley and Diana Barry accidentally stumbled upon her home, Miss Lavendar welcomed them warmly and formed an immediate, lasting bond with Anne. After discovering that Anne was the schoolteacher of Paul Irving—the son of her former fiancé Stephen Irving—she eventually agreed to meet the boy. She quickly grew fond of Paul, entertaining him at her home and treating him as a particular friend.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P31](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0031), [v2 c21 P36](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0036), [v2 c21 P38](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0038), [v2 c21 P44](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0044), [v2 c21 P83](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0083), [v2 c22 P7](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0007), [v2 c23 P23](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0023), [v2 c23 P26](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0026), [v2 c23 P29](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0029), [v2 c23 P34](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0034), [v2 c27 P63](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0063)_

## Background by volume

- Daughter of Mr. Lewis, who built the old stone house in Grafton eighty years prior  <sub>[v2 c22 P7](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0007)</sub>
- Named Lavendar by her father because he loved the scent of lavender associated with meeting her mother  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>
- Was considered a great beauty in her youth  <sub>[v2 c22 P3](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0003)</sub>
- Formerly engaged to Stephen Irving twenty-five years ago before a quarrel led to their separation  <sub>[v2 c21 P36](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0036), [v2 c22 P9](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0009)</sub>
